summary_result: Gazebo small/medium/large scenes: SR 100/92/80% with 0.2/0.6/1.2 collisions versus CityWalker 100/85/80% with 1.2/3.4/4.5, success within 10 m.
summary_limitation: The authors state limitations in scalability, robustness under extreme lighting or weather, and long-horizon consistency.

title: G-DRAGON: Geospatial Reasoning and Dynamic Planning for Retrieval-Augmented Outdoor Navigation
platform: Agilex Scout Mini UGV (drive type not recorded in the legacy card); NVIDIA Nova Carter UGV in Isaac Sim
sensors: RoboSense Helios16P 16-beam LiDAR, Intel RealSense D455F RGB-D camera, IMU, WheelTec G70 GPS
compute: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB onboard; Qwen2.5-14B on a local edge server for the initial behavior tree; latency not reported
summary_result: Isaac Sim Task 1 (building, 5 m): SR 100% / 95.56% at 300 / 800 m versus OPEN 77.78% / 26.67%; NoMaD fails at long range.
summary_limitation: The authors state that the system still needs a local network link to an edge server to obtain the initial behavior tree.

title: OpenIN: Open-Vocabulary Instance-Oriented Navigation in Dynamic Domestic Environments
platform: Autolabor robot (model and drive type not stated; four wheels visible in Fig. 6); simulated agent in Habitat on Gibson scenes
sensors: RGB-D camera (Azure Kinect DK on hardware) plus text and optional image instruction; Livox Mid-360 LiDAR for SLAM pose on hardware
compute: not reported; GPT-4o queried for carrier selection, image comparison, and image-to-text; no timing reported
summary_result: In 20 Habitat five-target tasks, fifth-target SR was 60-100% versus at most 60% for VLFM and OpenFMNav variants; all five targets in sequence succeeded in 0-60% per scene.
summary_limitation: On the real robot, missing depth on low-reflectivity or small objects and motion blur, which clean simulation avoids, plus occlusions or blind spots, caused CRSG update or recognition failures.

title: Uni-NaVid: A Video-based Vision-Language-Action Model for Unifying Embodied Navigation Tasks
platform: quadruped robot in the real-world demonstrations (model not reported); simulated agents in the benchmarks
sensors: monocular RGB video
compute: remote server with an NVIDIA A100 GPU; about 0.2 s to generate the next four actions
summary_result: R2R Val-Unseen in simulation: SR 47.0% and SPL 42.7 versus NaVid 37.4% and 35.9, with RGB-only input.
summary_limitation: The authors state that the model covers four fixed tasks and predicts only short-horizon discrete actions; smooth continuous motion is future work.

title: LeLaN: Learning A Language-Conditioned Navigation Policy from In-the-Wild Video
platform: prototype mobile robot on an iRobot Roomba base (Fig. 9); Unitree Go1 quadruped in qualitative cross-embodiment tests only
sensors: single RGB image from the front fisheye lens of a Ricoh Theta S, plus a text instruction
compute: Nvidia Jetson Orin AGX onboard; 0.054 s to generate one action
summary_result: With targets visible at the start, LeLaN reached within 0.2 m in 89% of 150 real-robot trials versus 67% for the strongest baseline, at 0.054 s per action onboard.
summary_limitation: The policy confuses identical objects under spatial instructions, and the authors call its reaching rate with obstacles (0.60 in 15 experiments, with J_col) insufficient for practical use.

title: DualMap: Online Open-Vocabulary Semantic Mapping for Natural Language Navigation in Dynamic Changing Scenes
platform: unnamed wheeled robot and unnamed quadruped sharing a LiDAR and RGB-D mount (Fig. 6a); Habitat agent on HM3D scenes in simulation
sensors: RGB-D camera; LiDAR used by Fast-LIO2 for external pose
compute: NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU and Intel i7-12700KF CPU; 0.276 s per frame on Replica
summary_result: In Habitat object navigation, DualMap reaches 70.5% average success in static scenes, 64.8% with in-anchor relocation, and 60.3% with cross-anchor relocation.
summary_limitation: The authors state that DualMap relies on external localization, does not model human-object interactions, and degrades outdoors because of higher sensor noise.

title: VLM-Social-Nav: Socially Aware Robot Navigation Through Scoring Using Vision-Language Models
platform: Turtlebot 2 (TurtleBot is differential-drive by the vocabulary definition) with Velodyne VLP-16, Zed 2i, and a laptop
sensors: Zed 2i RGB camera; Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR
compute: laptop with Intel i7 CPU and RTX 2080 GPU; GPT-4V queries with 2-3 s average response time
summary_result: Over four indoor social scenarios with 21 runs each, VLM-Social-Nav improves average success by at least 27.38% and average collision rate by 19.05% over DWA and behavior cloning.
summary_limitation: The authors state that GPT-4V responses take 2-3 s, which can be problematic in more dynamic scenarios, and that robot experiments were conducted only indoors.

title: OPEN: Lightweight Map-Based Semantic Navigation for GPS-Free Last-Mile Delivery
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
platform: unnamed wheeled campus robot with Logitech RGB camera, Livox MID-360, and GPS for ground-truth logging (Fig. 8); simulated differential-drive four-wheel robot in Gazebo
sensors: monocular RGB camera (Logitech); Livox MID-360 LiDAR
compute: AMD R9-7945HX with RTX 4060 for the benchmark; edge-side large model on an RTX 4090D (24 GB)
summary_result: In Gazebo residential scenes, OPEN reaches 100% success in small and medium scenes and 80% in the large scene, versus 40%, 20%, and 0% for ViNT and NoMaD.
summary_limitation: The authors state that OSM geometry can deviate from the road network, that LLM task planning fails through hallucination and output-format violations, and that indoor scenes are out of scope.

title: VLFM: Vision-Language Frontier Maps for Zero-Shot Semantic Navigation
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Boston Dynamics Spot with arm (real world); Habitat simulated agent (benchmarks)
sensors: RGB-D camera and planar odometry (simulation); Spot gripper RGB camera, Spot body depth cameras, and ZoeDepth monocular depth (real world)
compute: real-world models on a laptop RTX 4090 MaxQ Mobile GPU with 16 GB VRAM, "real-time"; no per-frame timing; simulation hardware not reported
summary_result: Habitat ObjectNav SPL/SR, success = STOP within 1 m in 500 steps: 52.2/84.0 Gibson, 30.4/52.5 HM3D, 17.5/36.4 MP3D versus SemUtil 40.5/69.3, ESC 22.3/39.2 (HM3D), 14.2/28.7 (MP3D).
summary_limitation: The authors assume targets are visible from the default camera height and the value map is task-specific; single-floor support fails 14.6% (HM3D) and 9.6% (MP3D) of episodes.

title: Hierarchical Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Language-Grounded Robot Navigation
platform: Boston Dynamics Spot (real two-story office); Habitat agent on HM3DSem
sensors: Azure Kinect RGB-D camera; 3D LiDAR for FAST-LIO2 poses with loop closure
compute: not reported (CLIP ViT-H-14, SAM, DBSCAN, GPT-3.5 queries; no CPU or GPU, mapping or query time)
summary_result: Real Spot, two-story office: object queries retrieved 29/41 (70.7%) and navigated 23/41 (56.1%); storage 1493 MB versus 6068 MB for VLMaps over eight scenes.
summary_limitation: The authors state that graph construction is time-consuming and unsuitable for real-time mapping, and that the method assumes a static environment.

title: Safe-VLN: Collision Avoidance for Vision-and-Language Navigation of Autonomous Robots Operating in Continuous Environments
platform: Habitat VLN-CE agent modeled as a 1.5 m mobile robot with simulated panoramic RGB-D; no drive type and no physical chassis
sensors: simulated panoramic RGB-D (12 RGB and 12 depth cameras); depth-derived 2D LiDAR occupancy mask
compute: not reported; the JPS-based navigator takes eight times longer than Safe-VLN on val-unseen
summary_result: On R2R-CE in Habitat, Safe-VLN raises SR and SPL over ETPNav and reduces navigation collisions; a JPS-based navigator takes eight times longer on val-unseen.
summary_limitation: The authors leave real-robot deployment, sim-to-real transfer, and training with real observations to future work; all results come from Habitat.

title: Can an Embodied Agent Find Your “Cat-shaped Mug”? LLM-Based Zero-Shot Object Navigation
platform: TurtleBot 2 (TurtleBot is differential-drive by the vocabulary definition); RoboTHOR agent in simulation
sensors: RGB-D camera (model not named); depth costmap via RTAB-Map and costmap_2d
compute: not reported; GPT-3 queried through prompts
summary_result: On a real TurtleBot 2, LGX reaches 54.2% success versus 27.8% for GLIP-on-Wheels and 6.9% for random exploration; on RoboTHOR, 35.0% versus 27.5% for OWL-CoW.
summary_limitation: The authors state that failure cases remain, especially when the LLM incorrectly localizes the target object, and that SR and SPL are weakly informative for zero-shot navigation.

title: Socially compliant mobile robot navigation via inverse reinforcement learning
venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
platform: autonomous robotic wheelchair with onboard laser range finders (no drive type in the legacy extraction)
sensors: laser range finders (Monte Carlo localization and a laser-based people tracker)
compute: not reported
summary_result: In simulation over ten hallway scenarios, the learned policy keeps 0.34 m minimum clearance, while time-configuration A* with a 0.8 m minimum distance is blocked 60% of the time.
summary_limitation: The authors assume cooperative agents and state that settings such as evacuations would need game-theoretic modeling.

title: Fault-Tolerant Multimodal Localization of Multirobots on Matrix Lie Groups
platform: three AgileX LIMO robots in Ackermann mode
sensors: MPU6050 IMU, wheel encoders, ORBBEC Dabai camera and ArUco markers
compute: NVIDIA Jetson Nano; measured latency and bandwidth not recorded
summary_result: Three fusion tests report fused ANEES of 0.85/0.99/0.89, treating 1500 time steps as independent realizations rather than repeating trials.
summary_limitation: The three-robot tests do not cover common-prior double counting, which requires at least four robots.

title: LiteFT-PR: Lightweight and Fault-Tolerant LiDAR-Camera Fusion Network for Robust Place Recognition via Model Distillation
platform: campus UGV; drive type not recorded
sensors: surround-view RGB and LiDAR; RTK ground truth for campus data
compute: Intel i9-12900K, 32 GB RAM, RTX 2080 Ti; reported runtime 12.72 ms
summary_result: On corrupted nuScenes BS/SON, LiteFT-PR Recall@1 is 97.26%/96.38% versus LCPR 80.55%/82.59%, while clean-data comparisons favor LCPR.
summary_limitation: Explicit author limitations were not recorded; the legacy review restricts timing evidence to desktop GPU retrieval rather than onboard closed-loop navigation.

title: Fault-Tolerant Trajectory Tracking for Unmanned Ground Vehicles via Virtual Error-Based Prescribed Performance Control
platform: Unnamed differentially driven UGV model (text description retained from the legacy extraction)
sensors: Heading and wheel-speed measurements; position assumed perfectly measured
compute: No processor or implementation timing recorded
summary_result: In numerical circular tracking with injected sensor faults, the legacy extraction reports position error below 0.02 m after 10 s.
summary_limitation: Perfect position measurement is assumed despite faults in heading and wheel-speed measurements.

title: Real-time kinematics-based sensor-fault detection for autonomous vehicles using single and double transport with adaptive numerical differentiation
platform: Yahboom aluminum-alloy Ackermann robot car chassis with Holybro Pixhawk 6C and M9N GPS; Readytosky S500 quadcopter with Holybro Pixhawk 4
sensors: position from the PX4 EKF (GPS, IMU) as a radar substitute, plus motion capture for the quadcopter; rate gyros; accelerometers; magnetometer heading (rover) or IMU attitude (quadcopter)
compute: computer and runtime not reported; 0.01 s sample time in simulation; 1000-step trailing window
summary_result: On recorded Ackermann-rover logs with injected faults, KSFD's six-metric pattern isolated a 1.0 m white-noise position fault and a harmonic z-gyro fault, one run each; no detection rates.
summary_limitation: Isolation assumes at most one faulty sensor; two simultaneous faults are only flagged, and statistical cutoff thresholds and onboard fault-tolerant integration are left to future work.

title: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control of Wheeled Mobile Robots With Multiple Actuator Faults and Saturation
platform: 120 kg industrial WMR with two driven wheels (legacy description)
sensors: wheel encoders and velocity feedback; LiDAR-based localization
compute: industrial computer, Qt/C++; CPU and control timing not reported
summary_result: Under injected faults, maximum mixed tracking-error norms were 31.4 versus 83.2/83.3 on curves and 22.2 versus 96.2/60.9 on straight paths, all multiplied by 10^-3.
summary_limitation: The controller requires positive remaining actuator effectiveness and a positive lower bound on the effectiveness-saturation product.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Real-Time Visual Anomaly Detection With Conformal Prediction in Dynamic Indoor Environments
platform: Scout Mini Pro in a university hallway; drive type not recorded
sensors: Intel RealSense D435 RGB; mounted Velodyne LiDAR not fused
compute: NVIDIA Jetson Xavier AGX; measured FPS, latency, and memory not recorded
summary_result: At alpha = 0.05, the hallway detector reports precision 0.9505, recall 0.3097, and false-positive rate 0.0308 on the local test set.
summary_limitation: The conformal guarantee assumes exchangeability and controls normal-sample false alarms, rather than anomaly recall.

title: Safe Control for Nonlinear Systems Under Faults and Attacks via Control Barrier Functions
platform: abstract feedback-linearized WMR model; separate Boeing 747 lateral model
sensors: abstract position/velocity channels; trusted noise-free WMR heading
compute: QP with EKF bank; CPU, solver period, and latency not recorded
summary_result: In illustrated WMR and Boeing numerical cases, the proposed controller preserves safety while residual-triggered reconstruction baselines cross the constraints.
summary_limitation: Candidate fault sets are known and disjoint; joint sensor-actuator attacks remain future work, and the actuator theorem uses a separate noise-free model.

title: Adaptive ergodic search with energy-aware scheduling for persistent multi-robot missions
platform: Orin DevQuad quadrotor mission agents; ground rover is a supporting mobile charging station
sensors: external Vicon pose; EKF prediction of charging-station position
compute: Orin NX on quadrotors, Raspberry Pi on rover, unspecified central host; 600 +/- 150 ms for three-agent hardware
summary_result: In four-quadrotor simulation, RmeSch reports eight returns with zero interval or minimum-energy violations; hardware demonstrations assume instantaneous recharging.
summary_limitation: Central-node failure recovery supports safe return but cannot ensure task continuity; experiments assume instantaneous recharging.

title: The Persistent Robot Charging Problem for Long-Duration Autonomy
platform: Simulated heterogeneous UAV fleet
sensors: No sensor model; known charging and operating durations
compute: Ubuntu 20.04 NUC, Intel i7-6770HQ, 32 GB RAM; Gurobi; TPWS under 0.01 s on evaluated instances
summary_result: In a two-station simulation, selecting UAVs 1, 2, and 7 yielded 58 aggregate flying minutes per 36-minute cycle.
summary_limitation: Known integer charging and operating times, full-charge cycles, and a common charging depot constrain the scheduling model.

title: Real-Time Out-of-Distribution Failure Prevention via Multi-Modal Reasoning
platform: custom quadrotor with Jetson Nano, Realsense D435, and PX4 (closed loop); ANYmal Generation D quadruped (recorded data); drone agent in CARLA (simulation)
sensors: RGBD camera (Realsense D435) with open-vocabulary detection; motion capture for drone pose
compute: Jetson Nano on the quadrotor; safety inference 0.011 s and reach-avoid planning 1.28 s per fallback; foundation-model queries 3.68-15.65 s run ahead of time
summary_result: In CARLA rooftop-landing fallbacks, FORTRESS had 92.2% successful and 7.8% no-plan rates versus 40.0% successful and 60.0% unsafe for AESOP; trial count not stated.
summary_limitation: The authors write the semantic fallback strategies by hand and map unsafe semantics to static, fixed-radius avoidance regions without dynamic or terrain-specific constraints.

title: CODEI: Resource-Efficient Task-Driven Co-Design of Perception and Decision Making for Mobile Robots Applied to Autonomous Vehicles
platform: Smart Fortwo, Chrysler Pacifica, and Mercedes-Benz C63 catalog meshes; nuScenes vehicle data
sensors: Velodyne and Ouster LiDAR catalog; Basler and FLIR RGB cameras; nuScenes perception data
compute: ETH Zurich Euler cluster; catalog compute choices range from Jetson Nano to AGX Orin
summary_result: Across 205 urban scenarios at 30 and 50 km/h, the legacy extraction records increasing resource demand as task complexity increases.
summary_limitation: Filtering, sensor fusion, and case studies beyond autonomous vehicles are left for future work.

title: ERPoT: Effective and Reliable Pose Tracking for Mobile Robots Using Lightweight Polygon Maps
platform: Eagle 204AKZ and YUHESEN FR-09; drive type not recorded
sensors: LiDAR-only tracking; GPS and IMU used for self-dataset ground truth
compute: Intel Core i7-11800H, 32 GB RAM; Ubuntu 20.04, ROS Noetic; runtime values not extracted
summary_result: On a self-recorded sequence 1.5 years after mapping, the legacy extraction records ERPoT tracking while HDL_localization and SM_MCL fail.
summary_limitation: Ground segmentation can fail on uneven terrain or low-obstacle clutter, degrading tracking.

title: A GP-based Robust Motion Planning Framework for Agile Autonomous Robot Navigation and Recovery in Unknown Environments
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Clearpath Jackal UGV (simulation and hardware); Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped (one hardware case)
sensors: 270-degree 2D LiDAR (simulation); Velodyne LiDAR (Jackal) and Ouster LiDAR (Spot) with Gmapping for map and state
compute: planner front-end under 1 ms, back-end typically over 100 ms, GP inference under 10 ms; processor not reported
summary_result: In 120 Gazebo runs (four room worlds, three goals, 10 runs each), success with recovery was never below without, for example 0.8 versus 0.3 (1 m doorways, dense, goal 0).
summary_limitation: No limitation is stated by the authors; future work lists distributional learning, planner switching, and dynamic obstacles, and hardware evidence is two snapshot case studies.

title: Fault-Tolerant Prescribed Performance Control of Wheeled Mobile Robots: A Mixed-Gain Adaption Approach
platform: Unnamed differentially driven WMR model (legacy text description)
sensors: No sensing stack recorded; high-frequency measurements required for implementation
compute: MATLAB Simulink, Bogacki-Shampine integration; 0.01 s step, 60 s horizon
summary_result: In numerical circular tracking under partial actuator loss, the legacy extraction reports position error below 0.02 m after 10 s.
summary_limitation: Errors are bounded within envelopes rather than exactly compensated; high-rate sampling and gain tuning are required.

title: Learning Self-Supervised Traversability With Navigation Experiences of Mobile Robots: A Risk-Aware Self-Training Approach
platform: Unnamed two-wheeled differential-drive urban robot (text, p. 5)
sensors: Downward-tilted Velodyne VLP-16; LIO-SAM footprint projection; proprioceptive label consistency
compute: Not recorded in the legacy extraction; not verified.
summary_result: The legacy experiments use about ten minutes of manually driven training per site at a mean 0.9 m/s; performance values were not extracted.
summary_limitation: Highly unstructured terrain is beyond the experimental robot’s operational capability.

title: User feedback and remote supervision for assisted living with mobile robots: A field study in long-term autonomy
platform: Giraff-X socially assistive robot (MoveCare system), 10 robots analyzed in older adults' apartments in Milan and Badajoz
sensors: Hokuyo URG 2D LiDAR (navigation), two Orbbec RGB-D cameras (obstacle avoidance and user detection), visual docking landmark; home IoT PIRs, door sensor, and room microphones
compute: on-board computer and NVIDIA Jetson TX2 labeled in Fig. 3; onboard navigation assumed; not described; VC, speech services, and MLS run in the cloud over MQTT; no runtimes reported; MLS snapshots every 30 min
degradation_observed: visual-degradation, dynamic-objects, scene-change, actuator-fault, sensor-fault, communication-delay-loss, communication-partition, energy-limit
summary_result: Across 10 homes and 132 robot-weeks, 86.46% of attempted WM, SQ, and REM interventions succeeded, and the robots lost localization 455 times over 13883.42 m.
summary_limitation: Autonomous recovery from idle-time events was often impossible, causes of lost localization were not ascertained, and unstable home internet delayed speech and caused the only drop-out.

title: Safety-Quantifiable Line Feature-Based Monocular Visual Localization With 3D Prior Map
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
platform: campus UGV (drive type unspecified); EuRoC aerial and CARLA vehicle data are additional settings
sensors: monocular images and IMU; prior 3D line map; HDL-32E LiDAR plus IMU construct campus reference/map
compute: Intel Core i9-12900K desktop, Ubuntu 20.04, ROS/C++; feature matching depends on prior-map size
summary_result: Recorded ground-robot and aerial-data experiments compare localization errors and empirical protection-level coverage; the computed protection level is not used to drive recovery.
summary_limitation: Protection-level coverage depends on measurement covariance and feature geometry; the study predicts estimation errors while planning and operational alert thresholds remain future work.

title: GSON: A Group-Based Social Navigation Framework With Large Multimodal Model
platform: two-wheeled nonholonomic mobile robot (p. 5)
sensors: 2D LiDAR and two RGB cameras
compute: processor/location not established in selected sections; dense-crowd LMM inference typically 1.5-2 s
summary_result: GPT-4o achieves 86.6% acceptable grouping on 100 scenes; hardware comparisons report lower social disturbance with modest navigation-time and jerk tradeoffs.
summary_limitation: Dense-crowd inference delay and occlusions reduce responsiveness and grouping accuracy; binary social-group avoidance lacks context-dependent flexibility.

title: Unpacking Failure Modes of Generative Policies: Runtime Monitoring of Consistency and Progress
venue: Proceedings of The 8th Conference on Robot Learning
platform: holonomic mobile base with Kinova Gen3 7-DoF arm (p. 23)
sensors: fixed external ZED 2; motion capture for mobile-base pose
compute: local policy/STAC hardware unspecified in selected sections; cloud VLM mean response 14.0 s
summary_result: Sentinel achieves 95% detection accuracy on 10 successful and 10 failed real-world chair-tucking rollouts; recovery outcomes are not evaluated.
summary_limitation: The method has no formal guarantee on detecting failures, and the STAC false-positive guarantee does not certify the VLM ensemble.

title: Perceive With Confidence: Statistical Safety Assurances for Navigation with Learning-Based Perception
venue: Proceedings of The 8th Conference on Robot Learning
platform: Unitree Go1 quadruped
sensors: ZED 2i RGB-D point clouds and vision-inertial odometry
compute: onboard ZED Box, 8-core ARM and 16 GB Orin NX; filter-only runtime 0.00025 s
summary_result: PwC was safe in 90% of hardware trials across 30 static chair environments; CP-avg collided in half its trials.
summary_limitation: The assurance assumes static obstacles and same-distribution environment sampling, with known state and a downstream safe planner.

title: Failure-Aware Multi-Robot Coordination for Resilient and Adaptive Target Tracking
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
platform: Crazyflie drones tracking Yahboom ROSMASTER X3 ground vehicles
sensors: range and bearing target observations; inter-robot communication; hardware sensing implementation not specified in targeted pages
compute: ForcesPro nonlinear solve and velocity control at 10 Hz; drone attitude control at 500 Hz; processor/solver location not reported
summary_result: Across six simulated failure scenarios, adaptive tracking reportedly reduced target-estimation MSE versus vanilla and motion-primitive controls; staged hardware trajectories have no tabulated MSE.
summary_limitation: The authors identify dynamic danger zones, partial degradation, and more realistic failure models as future work.

title: C-CBF: Communication-Aware Control Barrier Functions for Resilient Multi-Robot Connectivity
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
platform: abstract 2D double-integrator agents; ArduPilot quadrotors in network-in-the-loop simulation

compute: QPs on Intel i9-13900K PC CPU; network-in-the-loop controller at 10 Hz and QP solve below 10 ms
summary_result: In an eight-quadrotor network-in-the-loop simulation, the controller ran at 10 Hz with QP solves below 10 ms during jammer stress.
summary_limitation: The authors state that velocity-level guarantees, model-dependent link estimates, and network-in-the-loop tests require further physical validation.

title: CoVOR-SLAM: Cooperative SLAM Using Visual Odometry and Ranges for Multi-Robot Systems
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
platform: DLR Rover-1 (moving camera/UWB) and Rover-2 (stationary UWB anchor); KITTI car data split into four virtual agents

summary_limitation: The authors state that constant visual-odometry weighting may be suboptimal when it differs from true measurement covariance.

title: Event-Triggered Fault-Tolerant Tracking Control for Autonomous Ground Vehicle via Descriptor Reduced-Order Observer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
platform: Unnamed car-like AGV with steering front axle (bicycle model, p. 2; hardware-in-loop setup, p. 8)
sensors: Vehicle posture outputs in the model; physical sensor suite not established in the passages read
compute: Jetson Nano plus Windows/Ubuntu PCs over LAN; STM32 lower controller; individual timing not established
summary_result: The numerical example reports 85.64% triggering efficiency versus a 100% time-trigger rate; hardware-in-loop setpoint tests span five single and three sequential initial postures.
summary_limitation: The tested initial-posture range is narrow; complex real faults and extreme conditions remain to be investigated.

title: Switch-SLAM: Switching-Based LiDAR-Inertial-Visual SLAM for Degenerate Environments
platform: public Handheld, CERBERUS ANYmal, and SubT-MRS datasets; simulated Gazebo robot
sensors: 3D LiDAR, monocular camera, IMU; GNSS and loop closure excluded from main trajectory comparisons
compute: Intel i7-1165G7 CPU with Ubuntu; real-time dataset processing, no end-to-end navigation deadline
summary_result: On the selected Handheld degeneracy test, the proposed detector reports 0.96 accuracy and 0.99 recall; evaluation measures estimation rather than navigation recovery.
summary_limitation: Status changes near the threshold can be nonsmooth; the method uses buffering and interpolation, while broader real-world lighting and motion tests remain future work.

title: VL-TGS: Trajectory Generation and Selection Using Vision Language Models in Mapless Outdoor Environments
platform: Clearpath Husky; drive mechanics not independently checked in this targeted read
sensors: Velodyne VLP16, RealSense D435i, odometry velocity, and GPS current/target position
compute: laptop Intel i7 and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080; online GPT-4V selection takes 2-4 s
summary_result: GPT-4V responses take 2-4 s while DWA follows a previously selected approximately 10 m trajectory in the single-run-per-method outdoor experiment.

title: Visual localization in 3D maps: comparing point cloud, mesh, and NeRF representations

title: Extended Range of Localization Services via Formation-Controlled Mobile Ultra-Wideband Anchors

title: Bandwidth-Efficient Collaborative SLAM: Mutual Information for Data Selection and Finite-State Entropy for Lossless Compression
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering

title: Implicit Point-to-Voxel LiDAR-IMU SLAM

title: A Real-Time Degeneracy Sensing and Compensation Method for Enhanced LiDAR SLAM
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

title: Online IMU-Odometer Calibration Using GNSS Measurements for Autonomous Ground Vehicle Localization
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

title: Heterogeneous LiDAR dataset for benchmarking robust localization in diverse degenerate scenarios

title: NeuSE: Neural SE(3)-equivariant embedding for long-term object-based simultaneous localization and mapping
venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research

title: Efficiently closing loops in LiDAR-based SLAM using point cloud density maps
venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research

title: BIM-Loc: BIM-integrated discrepancy-aware LiDAR-based indoor localization
venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research

title: DCReg: Decoupled characterization for efficient degenerate LiDAR registration
venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research

title: SCALE: Self-Correcting Visual Navigation for Mobile Robots via Anti-Novelty Estimation
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

summary_limitation: More challenging or unknown environments remain future work (p. 6).

title: Mobile Robot Navigation Using Hand-Drawn Maps: A Vision Language Model Approach
platform: Clearpath Jackal with ZED Mini in campus indoor/outdoor user studies; wheeled/legged photorealistic simulation (pp. 5-6).

title: VLM-GroNav: Robot Navigation Using Physically Grounded Vision-Language Models in Outdoor Environments
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

title: Lifelong Autonomous Improvement of Navigation Foundation Models in the Wild

title: Velociraptor: Leveraging Visual Foundation Models for Label-Free, Risk-Aware Off-Road Navigation
platform: Off-road wheeled driving on a long test loop and separate staged OOD-obstacle course, with safety-operator corrections (pp. 7-8).
sensors: Camera visual-foundation-model features and LiDAR geometry projected to bird-eye maps
compute: Learned map construction and MPPI control; exact deployed processor/complete latency not retained from selected passages.

title: Mobility VLA: Multimodal Instruction Navigation with Long-Context VLMs and Topological Graphs
platform: Wheel-based mobile manipulator with MPC obstacle avoidance and a teleoperated demonstration tour (pp. 5-6).

compute: Long-context VLM high-level frame retrieval with offline topological graph and local waypoint policy; complete placement not retained (pp. 4, 8).

summary_limitation: No autonomous exploration; long high-level inference impedes interaction (p. 8).

title: SocialNav-SUB: Benchmarking VLMs for Scene Understanding in Social Robot Navigation
platform: Recorded human-centered robot navigation scenes; offline VQA and candidate-waypoint selection, not closed-loop robot control (pp. 4, 14).

compute: Multiple hosted/local VLMs compared offline; full per-model compute deployment not audited.
summary_result: Strong VLMs still trail rule-based and human-oracle scene understanding in the inspected benchmark.
summary_limitation: SCAND university-campus scope and a limited set of models/scenarios restrict benchmark coverage (p. 9).

title: Learning Smooth State-Dependent Traversability from Dense Point Clouds
platform: BeamNG.tech tire-deformation training/planning and a Scout Mini skid-steer demonstration; one risky alternative is virtual in the hardware course (pp. 6, 8, 16).

summary_limitation: Assumes a prebuilt fully observed point-cloud map; tire deformation is available only in simulation, and geometry-only smoothness assumptions have limits (p. 9).

title: Uncertainty-aware Accurate Elevation Modeling for Off-road Navigation via Neural Processes
platform: Polaris RZR off-road vehicle recordings from hills, desert and negative-obstacle scenes; elevation reconstruction evaluation (p. 5).

summary_result: Semantic neural processes jointly estimate elevation structure and predictive uncertainty on acquired off-road scenes.
summary_limitation: Predicted uncertainty needs calibration; range extrapolation, ego-elevation aggregation and fixed-grid downstream interfaces remain limitations (p. 9).

title: CARE: Enhancing Safety of Visual Navigation through Collision Avoidance via Repulsive Estimation
platform: LoCoBot on TurtleBot4 base, TurtleBot4 and RoboMaster S1 with per-platform parameters and low-speed constraints (pp. 6, 14).

compute: Depth estimation plus base navigation inference; complete physical compute placement not retained in selected passages.
summary_result: Trajectory correction improves collision-avoidance behavior within the evaluated speed/scenario conditions.

title: Towards Generalizable Safety in Crowd Navigation via Conformal Uncertainty Handling
platform: CrowdNav simulation and physical ROSMASTER X3 Mecanum robot using ROS2; physical model transferred without further fine-tuning (pp. 6, 8).

summary_result: Adaptive prediction uncertainty and constrained learning jointly guide crowd avoidance under tested distribution shifts.
summary_limitation: Missed detections, arbitrary-shaped static obstacles, residual OOD degradation and incomplete real-world shift coverage remain limitations (p. 9).

title: Geometrically-Constrained Radar-Inertial Odometry via Continuous Point-Pose Uncertainty Modeling
platform: Public 4D-radar datasets HeRCULES and SNAIL-Radar (outdoor vehicle sequences) and HKUST (indoor); carriers not inspected (pp. 5-6).

compute: Real-time operation and a computational-time analysis are reported (p. 8); processor not inspected in this reading.
summary_result: Joint point-pose uncertainty down-weights uninformative radar points; a planarity residual improves odometry only with the uncertainty-filtered map (p. 7).
summary_limitation: No limitation is stated in the inspected passages; refining local geometric assumptions is left for future work (p. 7).

title: Range-Aided LiDAR-Inertial Multi-Vehicle Localization and Mapping in Degenerate Environments
platform: Unmanned ground vehicles with differential steering and spring-damped suspension; two-vehicle open-square and three-vehicle complex-environment experiments (p. 8).

summary_result: Range constraints correct pose along the detected degenerate direction and support a low-drift shared map in degenerate multi-vehicle experiments (p. 13).
summary_limitation: Assumes LiDAR odometry remains non-degenerate in at least one horizontal direction (p. 7).

title: Robust Ground Constrained SLAM for Mobile Robot With Sparse-Channel LiDAR
platform: GroundRobotDataset recorded by a ground robot with sparse-channel LiDAR, IMU and RTK; drive type not stated in the inspected passages (p. 7, Fig. 6).

compute: Runtime section exists (p. 11); processor not inspected in this reading.
summary_result: Ground-normal constraints and intensity features reduce vertical drift and corridor degradation relative to baseline LiDAR SLAM on the authors' dataset (p. 11).
summary_limitation: Ground-change detection can fail when ground changes are below threshold, and only LiDAR and gyroscope are fused (pp. 10-11).

title: WING: Wheel-Inertial Neural Odometry With Ground Manifold Constraints
platform: KAIST Urban (cars) and NCLT (wheeled robot) datasets (p. 9).

summary_result: Learned IMU de-biasing, wheel-velocity correction and a continuous ground-manifold soft constraint outperform open-source interoceptive-only odometry baselines on two public datasets (p. 12).
summary_limitation: No limitation is stated in the inspected passages; low-order manifolds can reduce accuracy where the ground departs from the assumption (p. 11).

title: AirSLAM: An Efficient and Illumination-Robust Point-Line Visual SLAM System
platform: Public visual datasets with onboard, dynamic and low illumination (OIVIO, UMA-VI and others) and map-reuse sequences (pp. 10-14).

compute: 73 Hz on an i9-13900 CPU with RTX 4080 PC and 40 Hz on Jetson AGX Orin (p. 16).
summary_result: Point-line features and map reuse improve accuracy and relocalization under illumination changes; the system runs at 40 Hz on an embedded Jetson Orin (pp. 13-16).

title: CMRNext: Camera to LiDAR Matching in the Wild for Localization and Extrinsic Calibration
platform: Autonomous-driving datasets including KITTI; in-house self-driving perception car, quadruped and quadcopter recordings for zero-shot tests (pp. 7-8, 15).

summary_limitation: Trained only on driving data, not yet real time, and training requires ground-truth poses and correct intrinsics (p. 17).

title: Chamelion: Reliable Change Detection for Long-Term LiDAR Mapping in Transient Environments
platform: Custom LiDAR dataset from construction sites and a laboratory (prior map August 2024, scans October 2024) plus public data; carrier not inspected in this reading (p. 5).

summary_limitation: A fixed learned cross-visibility performs best when registration errors are small and voxel sizes match training (p. 8).

title: E2-BKI: Evidential Ellipsoidal Bayesian Kernel Inference for Uncertainty-Aware Gaussian Semantic Mapping
platform: Off-road and urban outdoor datasets including RELLIS-3D and an OffRoad dataset (pp. 5-7).

summary_result: Evidential semantics, Gaussian primitives and geometry-aligned kernels improve semantic mapping and uncertainty calibration under sparse inputs and limited training data (pp. 6-7).
summary_limitation: Predictive uncertainties require further calibration, and open-set extension is future work (p. 8).

title: Multi-Session Mapping and Long-Term Localization for Autonomous Vehicles Using Radar
platform: SNAIL-Radar and HeRCULES automotive-radar sequences with the ARS548 radar (p. 5).

compute: Processor not inspected in this reading.

title: OMCL: Open-Vocabulary Monte Carlo Localization
platform: Matterport3D sequences from VLMaps, Replica rooms and SemanticKITTI outdoor sequences (pp. 4-6).

summary_result: Open-vocabulary feature likelihoods enable cross-modal Monte Carlo localization and language-initialized global localization on indoor and outdoor datasets (pp. 5-7).

title: LiDAR Teach, Radar Repeat: Robust Cross-Modal Navigation in Degenerate and Varying Environments
platform: AgileX SCOUT 2.0 for closed-loop teach-and-repeat on a university campus; three platforms over 40+ km and six months (pp. 1, 12, 18).

title: Super4DR: 4-D Radar-Centric Self-Supervised Odometry and Gaussian-Based Map Optimization
platform: Public VoD and NTU4DRadLM datasets and a self-collected handheld and mobile-robot dataset in day, night and fog (pp. 9, 13, 16).

title: A Terrain-Adaptive $\epsilon$-Constraint MPC for Uneven Terrain Kinodynamic Planning
platform: Gazebo AgileX Scout Mini on two 3D meshes; physical Scout Mini outdoors and a four-wheeled JetAuto base (pp. 6-7).

title: MonoMPC: Monocular Vision Based Navigation With Learned Collision Model and Risk-Aware Model Predictive Control
platform: Clearpath Jackal with RealSense D435i used as RGB-only input; quadcopter demonstrations (pp. 6-7).

title: Off-Road Navigation via Implicit Neural Representation of Terrain Traversability
platform: AgileX Scout Mini with ZED 2i and Ouster OS1-32 in forest and grassland; training data from a Clearpath Husky A300 (p. 6).

title: HEIGHT: Heterogeneous Interaction Graph Transformer for Robot Navigation in Crowded and Constrained Environments

title: Safe Trajectory Generation for Nonholonomic Multi-Robot Systems: A Compensation-Based MPC Approach
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering

title: SCOPE: Stochastic Cartographic Occupancy Prediction Engine for Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Navigation
platform: Gazebo TurtleBot2 training data, SCAND Jackal and Spot recordings for prediction tests, and a hardware robot in a hallway (pp. 9, 17).

title: CoCoPlan: Adaptive Coordination and Communication for Multi-Robot Systems in Dynamic and Unknown Environments
platform: Simulated teams of up to 100 robots; hardware with four UGVs in an office and two UAVs with four UGVs in a disaster-response scene (pp. 2, 8).

title: Communication-Robust Asynchronous Distributed LiDAR Collaborative Smoothing and Mapping

title: Feedback-Guided Hierarchical Transmission for Multi-Robot Mapping Under Bandwidth Constraints

title: URGE: Efficient Decentralized Multirobot Exploration Guided by Unknown Regions Under Limited Communication
platform: Simulated Scout 2.0 robots with VLP-16; three real robots with Livox MID360 and Intel NUC in forest, parking-lot and tunnel scenes (pp. 11, 15).

title: riMESA: Consensus ADMM for Real-World Collaborative SLAM

summary_result: A robust incremental consensus-ADMM back end tolerates outliers, dropouts and latency and improves accuracy over prior back ends by a factor above seven on real-world datasets (p. 1).
summary_limitation: Convergence is provable only under restrictive conditions; shared-state identification is delegated to the front end (pp. 9, 11).

title: MEF-Explore: Communication-Constrained Multi-Robot Entropy-Field-Based Exploration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
platform: Gazebo TurtleBots and three physical TurtleBot2 robots on Kobuki bases with Intel NUC i5 and Velodyne LiDAR limited to 7 m (pp. 7, 13).
sensors: LiDAR occupancy mapping; low-rate position link and range-limited high-rate map link
compute: Intel NUC i5 on each robot (p. 13).
summary_result: Entropy-field exploration with implicit rendezvous gives 21.32% faster exploration and 16.67% higher success than the baseline in real-world experiments (p. 1).
summary_limitation: Heterogeneous teams and varying communication conditions are left for future evaluation (p. 15).

title: Sem-NaVAE: Semantically-Guided Outdoor Mapless Navigation via Generative Trajectory Priors
platform: Husarion Panther UGV with 64-channel Ouster LiDAR, RGB camera, IMU and GPS-RTK on 120-240 m campus and park routes (pp. 1, 5).
sensors: LiDAR, RGB camera, IMU, GPS-RTK
compute: NVIDIA RTX4060 laptop on the data-collection platform (p. 5); deployment placement not verified.
summary_result: CVAE candidate trajectories scored by open-vocabulary segmentation reach 90% success on 120-240 m routes, within 7% of a map-based upper bound (p. 1).
summary_limitation: Evaluation is limited to campus and park-like environments with few repeated trials per route (p. 8).

title: VAMOS: A Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Model for Capability-Modulated and Steerable Navigation
platform: Boston Dynamics Spot and the wheeled UW Hound in six indoor and outdoor environments; affordance models trained in Isaac Lab (pp. 5-6).
sensors: RGB images for the VLM planner; local elevation maps for the affordance model
compute: Inference at 1 Hz on an RTX 3080 laptop (p. 4).
summary_result: A VLM path planner re-ranked by an embodiment affordance model reaches 90% success over 270 trials, versus 53% for a modular stack and 27% for the best generalist (p. 1).
summary_limitation: The affordance model reasons only in geometric space (p. 8).

title: osmAG-LLM: Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation via Semantic Maps and Large Language Models Reasoning
platform: Habitat HM3D-SEM scenes and a campus building with five rooms; the physical robot navigates with ROS move_base (pp. 3, 5-7).
sensors: RGB-D camera; prior map scanned with a handheld 3D scanner app (p. 3)
compute: Not inspected in this reading.
summary_result: A lightweight semantic map with LLM priors and active detection outperforms dense open-vocabulary maps for relocated or unmapped objects; 27 of 30 real trials reach correct positions (pp. 7-8).
summary_limitation: Detection is limited by the categories of the underlying models; concealed objects are future work (pp. 4, 8).

title: VLN-Game: Vision-Language Equilibrium Search for Zero-Shot Semantic Navigation
platform: Habitat HM3D object-goal and language-goal tasks; Jackal with RealSense D455 and Ouster LiDAR for real-world deployment (pp. 9, 13).
sensors: RGB-D camera and odometry; LiDAR on the physical robot
compute: Perception and navigation modules on a computer with an RTX 3060 (p. 13).
summary_result: A 3D object-centric map with game-theoretic VLM disambiguation improves success and efficiency on HM3D object- and language-goal navigation (p. 13).
summary_limitation: Multi-view target identification and CLIP detection limits constrain navigation performance (p. 11).

title: OLiVia-Nav: An Online Lifelong Vision Language Approach for Mobile Robot Social Navigation
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Clearpath Jackal in real-world social navigation scenarios (p. 5).
sensors: Onboard RGB camera and 3D LiDAR (p. 2)
compute: Training on an NVIDIA H100 (p. 5); deployment compute not inspected.
summary_result: Distilled social-context embeddings track expert trajectories more closely and shorten personal-space violations versus DRL and VLM methods (p. 6).
summary_limitation: Larger crowded environments remain to be investigated (p. 6).

title: NORM-Nav: Zero-Shot Mobile Robot Navigation with Natural Language Behavioral Constraints
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Simulated four-wheeled differential-drive robot and a physical SCOUT 2.0 with Livox MID-360 and RealSense D455 (pp. 5-6).
sensors: LiDAR and RGB-D camera
compute: Onboard AMD R9-7945HX CPU with RTX 4060 GPU (p. 6).
summary_result: Language-derived geometric, semantic, directional and velocity costmap layers raise task success and align paths with human references in simulation; hardware tests demonstrate representative behaviors (pp. 6-7).
summary_limitation: No limitation is stated in the inspected passages; hardware evidence consists of representative demonstrations (p. 7).

title: Design and Implementation of Cloud–Edge Collaborative Mapping and Control System for Mobile Robots
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
platform: AgileX Hunter SE Ackermann robots with Jetson Orin NX over 5G; Kubernetes cluster for cloud services; Gazebo simulation (p. 11).
sensors: Onboard LiDAR and chassis data through ROS
compute: Cloud: four servers with AMD EPYC 7742 CPUs and two RTX 4080S GPUs; edge: Jetson Orin NX (p. 11).
summary_result: Offloading map construction and trajectory generation to a Kubernetes cloud while keeping MPC tracking and local avoidance onboard supports outdoor two-robot coordination and scaling (pp. 15-17).
summary_limitation: Planning and control algorithms are basic implementations; adaptive point-cloud transmission is future work (p. 19).

title: A Coordinated Approach to Control Mechanical and Computing Resources in Mobile Robots
platform: Wheeled rover with a DC motor, Jetson TX2 and DAVIS346 event camera in four environment-complexity settings (pp. 2-4, 11).
sensors: Event camera; motor power module and on-chip power sensors
compute: Jetson TX2 onboard with DVFS control (p. 4).
summary_result: Joint runtime control of motor speed and CPU voltage/frequency reduces overall energy consumption by up to 36.34% versus prior methods (p. 1).
summary_limitation: Communication energy is not considered; GPU acceleration and task migration are future work (pp. 3, 7).

title: Help Me Through: Imitation Learning Based Active View Planning to Avoid SLAM Tracking Failures
platform: Simulated indoor transitions for training and evaluation; a PeopleBot on a two-wheeled differential-drive Pioneer 3-DX with a laptop webcam in live mode (p. 14).
sensors: Monocular camera with ORB-SLAM3 tracking
compute: Timing analysis in Sec. V-F (p. 13); deployment on a connected laptop (p. 14).
summary_result: Human-supervised imitation learning lets active view planning cross room transitions without visual tracking failure where deep RL fails, after about 50 h of supervision (p. 1).
summary_limitation: Substantial human supervision is required; in the physical test the robot is teleoperated for path planning and obstacle avoidance (pp. 1, 14).

title: Multirobot Persistent Monitoring: Minimizing Latency and Number of Robots With Recharging Constraints
platform: Graph instances for patrolling, CVRP benchmark instances and a wildfire-monitoring graph built from satellite hotspot data (pp. 12-15).
sensors: None; graph-based planning
compute: Not inspected in this reading.
summary_result: An approximation algorithm and an orienteering heuristic minimize the number of robots that satisfy revisit-latency constraints with periodic depot recharging (pp. 5-16).
summary_limitation: Battery consumption may be stochastic in practice; multiple depots are future work (p. 16).

title: R-FAC: Resilient Value Function Factorization for Multirobot Efficient Search With Individual Failure Probabilities
platform: Canonical grid search environments in simulation and S30 searcher robots with embedded LiDAR and camera in a 12-room mock house (pp. 10-15).
sensors: Target detection assumed perfect in the model; LiDAR and camera on the S30 robots
compute: Server with RTX 3080 for simulations (p. 10).
summary_result: Log-sum-exp value factorization keeps search performance highest when one or several robots withdraw during execution (pp. 11-13).
summary_limitation: Assumes a perfect target sensor; malfunctioning robots simply quit the team (p. 15).

title: RADIUM: Predicting and Repairing End-to-End Robot Failures Using Gradient-Accelerated Sampling
platform: Simulated swarm search, formation control, power-grid, AV, drone and grasp problems; a 1/10th-scale car with vision in the loop (pp. 2, 11).
sensors: Simulated and real camera for the vision-in-the-loop car
compute: Threadripper 3990X CPU and RTX A4000 for rollouts (p. 8, Table I).
summary_result: Sampling failures from a failure posterior and repairing the policy yields up to five times higher hardware robustness of a vision-in-the-loop controller (p. 2).
summary_limitation: Requires a simulator with enough fidelity; failures not modeled by the simulator cannot be predicted (p. 13).

title: SubT-MRS Dataset: Pushing SLAM Towards All-weather Environments
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
platform: Aerial, legged and wheeled robots and RC cars share one sensor pack; carriers of individual challenge sequences are not stated in the inspected pages (pp. 1, 4).
sensors: Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR, four fisheye RGB cameras, FLIR Boson thermal camera, Epson IMU, optional depth camera (pp. 3-4)
compute: Sensor pack with an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier; the most accurate LiDAR challenge entry took 51.3 s per iteration (pp. 3, 7).
summary_result: Across 29 challenge submissions, average ATE is 1.61 m on mixed degradation versus 0.836 m on geometric degradation; no sensor-fusion entry met the success criteria (pp. 6-7).
summary_limitation: No limitation is stated by the authors; the limits they report concern the evaluated SLAM systems in caves, aggressive motion and mixed degradation (pp. 7-8).

title: RELLIS-3D Dataset: Data, Benchmarks and Analysis
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Clearpath Robotics Warthog on the Rellis Campus of Texas A&M University; drive type not stated in the inspected pages (pp. 1-2).
sensors: Ouster OS1 64-channel and Velodyne Ultra Puck LiDARs, Basler RGB camera, Nerian stereo camera, Vectornav VN-300 GNSS/INS (p. 2)
compute: Two onboard computers for control and data collection (p. 2); benchmark training hardware not inspected.
summary_result: Off-road benchmarks give 50.13% mIoU for GSCNN versus 74.7% on Cityscapes and 40.20% for SalsaNext versus 59.5% on SemanticKITTI (p. 5).
summary_limitation: All data come from a single outdoor facility, which limits diversity across splits; traversability labels are future work (p. 6).

title: STEP: Stochastic Traversability Evaluation and Planning for Risk-Aware Off-road Navigation
platform: Clearpath Husky in an abandoned subway (two levels, about 200 m x 100 m) and Boston Dynamics Spot in a lava tube; the simulation uses a differential-drive model (pp. 7-8).
sensors: Three Velodyne VLP-16 LiDARs on the Husky; one VLP-16 fused with Spot's RealSense data; LiDAR SLAM localization (p. 8)
compute: Entire autonomy stack on an onboard Intel Core i7 CPU; the traversability stack uses about one core (p. 8).
summary_result: In 50 Monte Carlo simulations, higher CVaR risk levels give longer paths with lower peak risk; Spot traverses 420 m of lava tube in 24 minutes (pp. 7-8).
summary_limitation: The authors name robustification of subcomponents and extension to higher speeds as future work (p. 8).

title: TartanDrive: A Large-Scale Dataset for Learning Off-Road Dynamics Models
venue: 2022 International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Modified Yamaha Viking ATV with throttle and steering servos driven by joystick; a human driver controls the brakes (p. 3).
sensors: Seven sensing modalities, including RGB images, heightmaps, IMU, shock travel and wheel RPM (pp. 1, 3)
compute: Not inspected in this reading.
summary_result: About 200,000 interactions in 630 trajectories; vision-based modalities help dynamics prediction more on a separate, more uneven evaluation set (pp. 1, 3, 6).
summary_limitation: Whether the improved dynamics prediction suffices for navigation over rough terrain remains to be seen; integration into a navigation stack is future work (p. 6).

title: EVORA: Deep Evidential Traversability Learning for Risk-Aware Off-Road Autonomy
platform: 0.33 m x 0.25 m RC car commanded by speed and steering angle (bicycle model) in an indoor arena; Boston Dynamics Spot outdoors; Husky forest data build the simulation (pp. 6, 14-15).
sensors: RealSense D455 on the RC car with Vicon pose; RealSense D455, Ouster OS0 LiDAR and built-in odometry on Spot (p. 15)
compute: RC car: onboard Intel Core i7 and RTX 2060, planning at 20 Hz; Spot: Jetson AGX Orin, planning at 5 Hz (pp. 15-16).
summary_result: Indoors, CVaR-Dyn with alpha 0.8 gives the best time-to-goal with 100% success over 5 races; avoiding OOD terrain removed human interventions outdoors (pp. 16-17).
summary_limitation: The pipeline relies on semantic segmentation, and the risk from perception uncertainty must be addressed separately (p. 18).

title: Kimera-Multi: Robust, Distributed, Dense Metric-Semantic SLAM for Multi-Robot Systems
platform: Clearpath Jackal UGVs recorded the Medfield and Stata outdoor datasets; EuRoC and photo-realistic simulations add further tests (pp. 12, 14).
sensors: Forward-facing RealSense D435i RGB-D camera and IMU (p. 14)
compute: Communication payloads and solution runtime are tabulated in Table II (p. 13); the machine was not identified in this reading.
summary_result: Under 70% synthetic outlier loop closures, GNC with robust initialization reaches 0.003 m ATE versus 2.24 m for PCM; outdoor trajectories reach 860 m per robot (pp. 4, 14).
summary_limitation: Experiments keep robots constantly in communication range; scenarios with intermittent communication are future work (p. 12).

title: LAMP 2.0: A Robust Multi-Robot SLAM System for Operation in Challenging Large-Scale Underground Environments
platform: Team CoSTAR datasets from Husky robots (described as wheeled, drive type not stated) and Spot quadrupeds; Huskies carry the majority of the four datasets (p. 5).
sensors: Three Velodyne LiDARs or a Hovermap on the Husky; one LiDAR or a Hovermap on Spot; LOCUS or Hovermap odometry (p. 5)
compute: Experiments ran on a laptop with an Intel i7-8750H (12 cores); during SubT the base station was an AMD Threadripper 3990X workstation (p. 5).
summary_result: On four subterranean datasets of up to 6 km combined, LAMP 2.0 achieves map errors below 4 m, and GNC rejects outliers more reliably than ICM (pp. 5-7).
summary_limitation: No limitation is stated by the authors; the evaluation replays recorded team data on a laptop running the centralized base-station software.

title: Heterogeneous Ground and Air Platforms, Homogeneous Sensing: Team CSIRO Data61's Approach to the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
platform: BIA5 ATR, SuperDroid LT2-F and CSIRO DTR tracked UGVs, CSIRO hexapod and Ghost Vision60 quadruped, and Emesent Hovermap UAVs; no wheeled robot (pp. 1-2, 6-7).
sensors: CatPack spinning-LiDAR payload with cameras on UGVs; Hovermap payload on UAVs; CO2 and Bluetooth/WiFi sensing (pp. 5, 8, 16)
compute: Each agent solves multi-agent SLAM onboard; ground vehicles run image inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Xavier in the CatPack (pp. 15, 21).
summary_result: The team detected 11 of 80 artifacts at the Tunnel Circuit, 15 of 80 at the Urban Circuit and 16 of 44 at its Cave event (pp. 31, 33, 37).
summary_limitation: At the Cave event, global paths and frontiers did not penalize difficult terrain enough; risk-based selection is follow-on work (pp. 35, 39).

title: Resilient and Modular Subterranean Exploration with a Team of Roving and Flying Robots
platform: Custom ground robots R1-R3 with four motor/wheel modules (drive type not stated) and drones; R3 can also take tracks (pp. 19, 28).
sensors: Perception payload with LiDAR, cameras (electro-optical, thermal), IMU and RealSense depth; communications node dropper on each ground robot (pp. 5, 7, 19)
compute: Not inspected in this reading.
summary_result: Tunnel Circuit winner and Urban Circuit runner-up, Team Explorer's two ground robots explored about 2 km and scored 13 artifacts on one tunnel day (pp. 1, 43).
summary_limitation: Added system complexity can reduce overall reliability; artifacts were missed when not in view of the detection cameras (pp. 51-52).

title: CERBERUS in the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
platform: Four ANYmal C SubT quadrupeds in the winning prize run, aerial scouts, and a tethered wheeled rover that served as a communication hub (pp. 2-3).
sensors: LiDAR and Alphasense Core visual-inertial cameras on all ANYmal robots; extra LiDARs, zoom and thermal cameras on Explorer units (p. 2)
compute: CompSLAM runs onboard each robot; M3RM multi-robot mapping runs centrally on the Base Station (pp. 4-5).
summary_result: In the Final Event prize run, the robots walked more than 1.7 km and reported 23 of 40 artifacts, winning on the tiebreaker with CSIRO Data61 (pp. 1-3).
summary_limitation: Small aerial robots have limited endurance; marsupial ferrying of an aerial robot by ANYmal was finalized only after the competition (p. 5).

title: Habitat-Matterport 3D Dataset (HM3D): 1000 Large-scale 3D Environments for Embodied AI
venue: Neural Information Processing Systems Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
platform: Simulated Habitat PointNav-v1 agent with RGB-D input, GPS+Compass localization and discrete 0.25 m and 10-degree actions; scans from a tripod-mounted Matterport Pro2 (pp. 4, 7).
sensors: Matterport Pro2 tripod-based depth sensor for the scans; the simulated agent receives 256 x 256 RGB-D and GPS+Compass readings (pp. 4, 7)
compute: PointNav agents trained with DD-PPO for 1.5 billion frames (p. 7); hardware not inspected.
summary_result: HM3D has 1,000 scenes and 112.5k square meters of navigable space; HM3D-trained PointNav agents reach 100% performance on the Gibson test set (pp. 1-2).
summary_limitation: Object semantics and physical attributes are left to future extensions, which would enable ObjectGoal navigation and rearrangement (p. 10).

title: LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Pre-Trained Models of Language, Vision, and Action
platform: Clearpath Jackal UGV in two outdoor suburban environments; drive type not stated in the inspected pages (pp. 5-6).
sensors: Onboard camera images and GPS observations collected while manually driving to build the graph (p. 6)
compute: Not inspected in this reading; the paper does not state in the inspected pages where GPT-3 is queried.
summary_result: Over 20 instructions covering more than 6 km, LM-Nav finds a successful walk for 85% and needs one disengagement, about 1 per 6.4 km (pp. 6-7).
summary_limitation: LM-Nav keeps only landmarks and drops verbs and other cues, and its navigation model is specific to outdoor navigation with the Jackal (p. 8).

title: GNM: A General Navigation Model to Drive Any Robot
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Deployed on a LoCoBot (Kobuki base), a Roomba-based Vizbot, a Clearpath Jackal and a DJI Tello held at 1 m height; quantitative tests use the Jackal and LoCoBot (p. 4).
sensors: Monocular RGB cameras (PCB-mounted fisheye on the deployed robots); training data pair images with commanded actions and local odometry (pp. 2, 4)
compute: Not inspected in this reading.
summary_result: Trained on 60 hours from 6 robots, one GNM policy controls four robots, including two unseen ones, and outperforms single-dataset policies by up to 5x (pp. 1, 4).
summary_limitation: The model does not account for differences in capabilities and assumes ground robots with a forward-facing RGB camera; the dataset could be much larger (p. 6).

title: ViNT: A Foundation Model for Visual Navigation
platform: Five platforms, among them a drone, a Go 1 quadruped, LoCoBot, Vizbot and Jackal; zero-shot exploration is reported for LoCoBot, Go 1, Vizbot and Jackal; drive types not stated (pp. 6-7).
sensors: Monocular camera images; onboard wheel odometry indoors and GPS or satellite imagery outdoors for goal heuristics (pp. 3, 6)
compute: Training on several multi-GPU workstations (p. 14); deployment hardware not inspected.
summary_result: Trained on over 100 hours from 8 robots, ViNT drives an unseen Go 1 quadruped zero-shot and reaches 80% CARLA success with under one hour of fine-tuning (pp. 4, 7-8).
summary_limitation: ViNT carries a heavier inference cost than simple convolutional networks, which challenges power-constrained platforms, and it assumes structural similarity across robots (p. 8).

title: ConceptGraphs: Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Perception and Planning
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: Clearpath Jackal UGV in the REAL Lab for navigation queries; Boston Dynamics Spot Arm for pick and place; Replica scenes for quantitative tests (p. 5).
sensors: RGB-D input for mapping; the Jackal carries a VLP-16 LiDAR and a forward-facing RealSense D435i camera (p. 5)
compute: SAM, CLIP, LLaVA and GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613); the authors note that LVLM and proprietary LLM inference costs may be significant (pp. 4, 6).
summary_result: An open-vocabulary 3D scene graph from 2D foundation models supports language queries; on the Jackal, an LLM redirects search after a target object is moved (pp. 4-6).
summary_limitation: Node captions inherit LVLM errors, small or thin objects are missed or duplicated, and LVLM and proprietary LLM inference costs may be significant (p. 6).

title: NoMaD: Goal Masked Diffusion Policies for Navigation and Exploration
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
platform: LoCoBot in six indoor and outdoor environments; drive type not stated in the inspected pages (pp. 4-5).
sensors: RGB observations of the past timesteps and an optional goal image (p. 3)
compute: The policy runs entirely on the edge with a 15x smaller model than the strongest baseline (p. 5); processor not identified in this reading.
summary_result: One goal-masked diffusion policy handles exploration and goal reaching in six real environments, improving over subgoal diffusion by over 25% with 15x fewer parameters (pp. 4-6).
summary_limitation: Goals are specified only as images, and high-level exploration uses a standard frontier strategy (p. 6).
